title: Netherlandish Proverbs

caption: One village, more than 100 proverbs acted out literally. How many do you still use today? #art #arthistory #painting #renaissance #history

slides.headline: This 1559 painting hides over 100 proverbs
slides.sub: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, Netherlandish Proverbs, 1559

slides.headline: The world turned upside down
slides.text: Bruegel starts with a warning. Up on the house, the globe hangs upside down: in this village, everything is backwards.

slides.headline: Nobody cares
slides.text: And the man in the window above? He relieves himself on that world. He couldn't care less.

slides.headline: The blue cloak
slides.text: Down in the square, a wife wraps her husband in a blue cloak. It means she is cheating on him, and he has no idea.

slides.headline: Banging his head
slides.text: Not far away, a man bangs his head against a brick wall, wasting his strength on the impossible.

slides.headline: Belling the cat
slides.text: Next to him, another tries to tie a bell on the cat. Brave, but a plan that rarely works.

slides.headline: Roses for the pigs
slides.text: Further along, someone throws roses to the pigs, giving his best to those who can't value it.

slides.headline: Too late
slides.text: And right beside him, a man fills in the well only after the calf has drowned. Here, every fix comes too late.

slides.headline: Your turn
slides.text: That was only seven. Over a hundred more are hiding in this village. Which one do you still use?
